answer.reason: Sodom's story has two chief events in the verses: its defeat and plundering by the eastern kings, and its destruction by fire and brimstone from the LORD.

clauses.english: was plundered by Chedorlaomer and the eastern kings, who took Lot captive
clauses.quote: they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah

clauses.english: was destroyed by brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven
clauses.quote: the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven

doubts: Left out the later verses that use Sodom as a comparison or warning (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Matthew, Jude, etc.), since figures of speech are not events.
Left out Rev 11:8, where Sodom is a spiritual name for another city.
Ezekiel 16 speaks of Sodom as a sister of Jerusalem and Samaria, which is a figure and not an event; it was not used.
The verses on the wickedness of the men of Sodom (GEN 13:13, GEN 19:4) describe character and an attempted deed, so they were not made clauses; the verses of GEN 19:7-21 were not provided.
